claims.claim: Hebrew keyboards are bilingual with the U.S. QWERTY layout on the same physical keys, which is why text typed with the wrong layout active can be recovered by key position.
claims.raw_snippet: Most [[Hebrew language|Hebrew]] keyboards are bilingual, with [[Latin script|Latin]] characters, usually in a U.S. [[QWERTY]] layout.
claims.verified_via: raw fetch of the article wikitext (action=raw)

claims.claim: The five Hebrew final letters (ך ם ן ף ץ) are used only at the end of a word, so a final letter in the middle of a 'word' is a strong signal of wrong-layout typing.
claims.raw_snippet: the modern Hebrew script has five [[letter (alphabet)|letters]] that have special [[final form]]s, ... called '''sofit''' ... form, used only at the end of a word
claims.verified_via: raw fetch of the article wikitext (action=raw)

claims.claim: Keyboard Fix is a free MIT-licensed Windows tool that flips selected text between the Hebrew and English layouts with Ctrl+CapsLock in any app, including terminals.
claims.raw_snippet: Typed a whole sentence in the wrong keyboard language? Select it, press `Ctrl+CapsLock`, done. ... Hebrew ↔ English layout fixer for Windows — works in every app.
